finding.text: The exit line differs from what the brief asked for: the brief wanted `{"pid":N,"exit":{code,signal}}` and the code writes `{"pid_exit":N,"code","signal"}` (Servex/SpawnLog.js:217). The change is better, because a search for `"pid":N` now finds only the start line, and Servex/doc/processes.md:382 explains it. But the completion line in session.jsonl never says it differs from the brief, so the parent should be told.

`SpawnLog.load()` (Servex/SpawnLog.js:200) copies the commit-charge math from `Global.commit_pct()` (Servex/agents/Global.js:411) instead of calling `servex.global?.commit_pct()`. Two copies of one rule can drift apart (law 6). It also adds a `page_file_mb` field the brief never asked for, and that field is always null.

finding.md was changed in a commit made straight on main (ea15a1fd9), outside the brief's file fence, before this branch is merged. Until the merge, its two new rows describe `pid`/`queued` lines that main never writes.

If an agent's task dir resolves but holds no session.jsonl or task.jsonl, the line is dropped without a trace (Servex/SpawnLog.js:231). It goes neither to that dir nor to the `spawns` log. Only a dir that fails to resolve falls back to `spawns`, which is what test 5 covers.

The sessions readme's search is `git grep` (public/framework/ai/sessions/readme.md:409). That only reads tracked files, so it misses pid lines in a session folder that isn't committed yet. The brief asked for `grep -r`, which has no such gap.

In Servex/readme.md:80, the link to doc/processes.md is still labelled "(closing a task leaves nothing running)". A reader scanning that index won't learn the doc now also answers "who started this pid".
